nodes.name: Cr,Co Codoped NiFe LDH Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Cr and Co codoped NiFe LDH nanocages synthesized using Cu₂O template through coordination etching (molar ratio ~5% each) based on previous work (Experimental, Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: we first synthesized Cr and Co codoped NiFe LDH nanocages using a Cu₂O template through coordination etching... both with a molar ratio of ~5%

unit_operations.name: Coordination Etching
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: synthesized Cr and Co codoped NiFe LDH nanocages using a Cu₂O template through coordination etching

nodes.name: Cr Release by Electrooxidation
nodes.procedure: In situ electrooxidation process applied to Cr,Co-NiFe LDH nanocages to release Cr as CrO₄²⁻ and form amorphous V_Cr,Co-NiFeOOH with Cr vacancies, confirmed by UV-vis and Pourbaix diagram.
nodes.source_text: Then an in situ electrooxidation process was applied to release Cr from Cr,Co-NiFe LDH and form V_Cr,Co-NiFeOOH with Cr vacancies. The leaching Cr exists in the form of CrO₄²⁻

unit_operations.name: Electrooxidation

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows octahedral nanocages with average side length of 700 nm, composed of many tiny grains.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2b shows octahedral nanocages of V_{\mathrm{Cr}} , Co-NiFeOOH with an average side length of 700~\mathrm{nm} , mostly the morphology of their precursor (Figures S10 and S11). These octahedra are composed of many tiny grains.

properties.description: Transmission Electron Microscopy image showing nanoparticles with scale bar 10 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern shows halo rings indicating amorphous nature of the catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SAED pattern with halo rings in Figure 2c suggests the amorphous nature, which is consistent with the X-ray diffraction (XRD) result in Figure S12.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping presents uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, Co, and O elements in amorphous V_Cr Co-NiFeOOH with no phase or element segregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mapping presents the uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, Co, and O elements in amorphous V_{\mathrm{Cr}} , Co-NiFeOOH...

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM image confirms the amorphous structure of V_Cr Co-NiFeOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image at the bottom of Figure 2c further confirms the amorphous structure of V_{\mathrm{Cr}} , Co-NiFeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES reveals atomic ratio of Ni:Fe:Co ~ 15:5:1 for V_Cr Co-NiFeOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) analysis in Table S1 reveals the atomic ratio of Ni:Fe:Co ∼ 15:5:1 for V_{\mathrm{Cr}} , Co-NiFeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: PAS shows three lifetime parameters with τ₁=179 ps (longer than 144 ps of precursor), τ₂, τ₃ confirming Cr vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figures 2d and S14 and Table S2 show the PAS results with derived lifetime parameters. There are three distinct lifetime parameters, τ₁,τ₂ and τ₃... the longer τ₁ (179 ps) for V_{\mathrm{Cr}} Co-NiFeOOH might come from positron annihilation in Cr vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge shifts to higher energy indicating increased Ni valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni K-edge of V_{\mathrm{Cr}} Co-NiFeOOH in Figure 2e shifts toward higher energy, manifesting a rise of Ni valence state in V_{\mathrm{Cr}} Co-NiFeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge shows increased Ni-O bond length and decreased Ni-O coordination number indicating metallic vacancy formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni-O bond length of V_{\mathrm{Cr}} Co-NiFeOOH is bigger than that of Cr,Co-NiFe LDH... it shows a decreased coordination number of Ni-O compared with Cr,Co-NiFe LDH (Table S3), further indicating the formation of a metallic vacancy.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p shows Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ ratio of 1.78 and 0.23 eV positive shift vs Co-NiFeOOH; confirms increased Ni/Co valence states post-activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the Ni 2p XPS spectrum in Figure 4a... The ratio of Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ increases from 0.33 of NiFeOOH to 1.78 of Co-NiFeOOH... a positive shift of 0.23 eV was observed for V_{\mathrm{Cr}} , Co-NiFeOOH compared with Co-NiFeOOH... The XPS spectra in Figure S18 further confirm the increased valence states of Ni and Co after activation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni L-edge sXAS shows increased intensity at 855.4 eV confirming higher Ni valence state after Co doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4b also confirms a higher Ni valence state after Co doping by increased intensity of the Ni L₃-edge peak of V_{\mathrm{Cr}} , Co-NiFeOOH at 855.4 eV.
